reviewer: Claude 2, independent; did not author the subject
discipline: Refute, do not confirm. The subject is a single-finding successor, so the attack ran on two fronts at once: whether the advertised repair is real against live bytes rather than against the finding text, and whether landing it moved anything the split predecessor already carried. The cited field of the cited artifact — g21-fixture-corpus.v1 authoredCatalog.executionRemains — was read in full and set character-for-character against the subject's recital, because a field-level citation that misstates its own source was the entire charge in the predecessor. Every digest recorded anywhere in the file was recomputed from disk in both the inline basedOn pairs and the flat recordedInputs ledger. A full structural diff of frozen v6 against v7 was taken key-by-key to expose anything smuggled alongside the repair, since a single-finding successor has no legitimate reason to move a measurement. Occupancy v4's controlling passProperty and corpus v1's whatIsNotAuthored were re-derived independently rather than inherited from v6 or from the v5/v6 review text. The on-disk g21.v1 fixture tree was listed and its payload digests recomputed to test the platform-copy remainder physically. Live file 08, live COORD, and the live G21 v3 corpus lists were resolved directly rather than accepted as paraphrase.
decisionRule: ACCEPT only at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX stand, so the verdict is ACCEPT.
codexStanding: docs/coop/artifacts/g21-leftover-join.v7.review-independent.codex.json was neither opened, listed, nor probed for existence. This verdict is Claude 2's alone. Disclosed departure: the verdict and count fields only — not the reasoning — of the frozen v5 and v6 Codex reviews were read, because the subject pins both as inputs and asserts their verdicts in basedOn.predecessorV5/V6 and in appliesFindingsOf.idCollisionNote, and those assertions are checkable claims about pinned bytes. Both reproduce as ACCEPT with empty blockers, mustFix and shouldFix. No Codex review of this subject informed this verdict.
reviewerDisclosure: This review occupies the Claude 2 slot, and that slot authored G21LJ-V6-SF1 — the sole finding this successor exists to land — as well as the independent reviews of g21-leftover-join v1 through v6 and of the corpus and occupancy artifacts this successor consumes. The bias is unusually strong and runs toward ACCEPT: confirming that one's own finding was honoured is the easiest possible reading, and the repair direction raised in that finding was written by this slot. It was countered three ways. First, the repair was tested against live corpus v1 bytes rather than against the finding's own description of them, so the standard applied is what the cited field says, not what the finding said it says. Second, a complete key-by-key diff of v6 against v7 was taken so that a correct repair could not launder an incorrect change travelling with it — the specific defect this bias would hide. Third, the v4-currency wording and the two-item proposedLaterWork form, both of which this slot disposed of as observations when reviewing v6, were re-examined on their merits against live D-241 rather than carried forward by prior disposition; both survive that re-examination, and both are recorded below as observations rather than findings for the same reasons that hold independently of the earlier disposition. This reviewer did not author the subject.

landedFindingAudit.detail: The finding offered two repair directions and the subject took the second: quote corpus v1's authoredCatalog.executionRemains as it stands, including host-projection goldens. The recital in obligations[3].reason is verbatim-exact against the live field. Live corpus v1 reads 'Qualification. Pinning authored bytes is not execution and is not SATISFIED. Candidate-buffer digest, subsequent-session view, and host-projection goldens remain G21 execution (D-056), not leftover-design.' and that string occurs in the subject's obligations[3].reason character-for-character following the citation 'corpus v1 authoredCatalog.executionRemains:'. Both limbs of the original charge are cured. The unsourced item is gone: 'Host-refusal observation' no longer appears as an asserted routing anywhere, and the only two occurrences of the substring 'refus' in the whole subject are negative guards — purpose's 'Do not fold an unsourced host-refusal observation into that field' and appliesFindingsOf.v6's 'Host-refusal observation is not folded into that field' — which state what was not done rather than doing it, in the same negative form the artifact's doesNot list uses throughout. The dropped item is restored and is no longer absent from every ledger: 'host-projection' occurs six times, including leftoverDesignOpenStanding, which now reads 'Candidate-buffer digest, subsequent-session view, and host-projection goldens remain qualification at OBL-G21-EXECUTION (D-056), not leftover-design', and obligations[4].reason, which now attributes the three-item routing to the corpus field by name. Every prohibition attached to the repair holds: no observation bytes are authored, NT-6 remains at obligations[3].remainingNotAuthored.dr133, perD002PlatformCopiesOfAuthoredNt1Nt2 remains alongside it, and the whole remainingNotAuthored object is byte-identical to v6's.

observationsNotFindings.whyNotAFinding: Re-examined on its merits at this version rather than carried by the disposition made at v6, and it survives. The phrase is the lineage's term of art for 'not the current remasurement, not recordable as a current leftover measurement', which is how v2's role uses it verbatim — 'Not recordable as a current leftover remasurement because file 08 moved and required-now is 28'. The subject states v4's standing consistently everywhere it matters: basedOn.predecessorV4.role records what D-196 actually did ('Recorded at D-196 as current G21 leftover-join'), remeasurementClause calls v4 'a historical measurement recorded at D-196', and doesNot entry 19 reads 'Does not record leftover-join.v4 as current after this successor is recorded', which presupposes rather than denies that v4 holds the recorded remainder until a successor displaces it. Nothing in the artifact reads v4 as displaced already, and nothing turns on the phrase: no measurement, no obligation and no remainder depends on it. The wording is byte-identical to frozen v6 and to the live record it is being tested against, so it is not a regression introduced by this repair.

decision.scopeOfAccept: Accepts g21-leftover-join.v7 as an independently reviewed CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED leftover remasurement that binds NOTHING. It is not a recording, does not make G21 QUALIFIED, does not SATISFY DR-114 or DR-133, and does not close leftover-design of OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING.
decision.rationale: The subject exists to land one SHOULD-FIX and it lands it exactly, by the stricter of the two repair directions offered: the cited field of corpus v1 is now quoted verbatim rather than paraphrased, the unsourced host-refusal term survives only as a negative guard, and the dropped host-projection goldens are restored to four separate fields. Both limbs of the original charge are cured with nothing left over. The repair is also clean: a full key-by-key diff against frozen v6 shows zero removed keys and no measurement moved, so the correct repair did not carry an incorrect change with it. Every digest the subject records reproduces from live bytes in both its ledgers; the fixture tree, occupancy v4's passProperty, corpus v1's whatIsNotAuthored, the live G21 v3 corpus lists, the DR-G21 status token, the gate owner, required-now 28, and the last COORD heading all resolve as stated. Every attack in the dispatch, plus four raised independently of it, is refuted against live bytes. Five observations are recorded and none rises to a finding: each is either byte-identical to the dual-tested predecessor, faithful to the live recording it echoes, or carries no measurement. Zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX stand.
